what_it_does: An Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) is a compact, high-speed index structure — think of it as a smart sorted dictionary — used in databases and key-value stores to look up records extremely fast. The problem is that many database operations touch the same tree nodes repeatedly (many lookups share a common path from the root), yet each operation re-traverses those nodes independently, wasting time. Concurrent reads and writes also require synchronization (locking) that adds overhead. DCART is a custom hardware accelerator that groups together requests targeting the same ART node so the shared path is traversed only once for a batch, and caches the most frequently visited nodes and their results on-chip to avoid re-reading from slower memory. The design is described as data-centric because the hardware is organized around the data access patterns of the tree rather than around a fixed compute pipeline.
